uni-env-core.title: Environmental Science and Engineering core
uni-env-core.description: Core environmental science and engineering: ecology, water and wastewater, air pollution control, solid waste and climate with EIA, with numericals and practical labs. Study companion; topics commonly taught in Indian degree programmes.

courses.title: Ecology: energy flow, populations and biodiversity indices
courses.summary: Trophic energy transfer, population growth and Shannon and Simpson diversity indices.

lessons.title: Lab: Energy up the food chain

scenes.text: A park ecologist in Kaziranga explains why top predators are few.
Energy shrinks at every trophic step.

steps.title: Ten percent rule
steps.body: Roughly 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level (the rest is lost as heat, respiration and waste). The real value varies from about 5 to 20%.

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: 10,000 kJ in producers → 1000 (herbivores) → 100 (carnivores) → 10 kJ (top carnivores).

steps.title: Mistake
steps.body: Energy flows one way and is not recycled; nutrients cycle.

activity.prompt: Producers fix 10,000 kJ. Using 10% transfer, how much reaches tertiary consumers (4th trophic level)?

lessons.title: Lab: Capstone – Carbon accounting and the EIA process

scenes.text: A company proposes a plant; the consultant first estimates CO₂ from coal.
Then she explains the EIA stages to the community.

steps.title: CO₂ from carbon
steps.body: Burning 1 kg C yields 44/12 = 3.667 kg CO₂. 1000 kg coal at 60% C → 600 kg C → 2200 kg CO₂.

steps.title: GWP
steps.body: CO₂-equivalent = mass × GWP. With a 100-year GWP of about 28 for methane (IPCC AR5), 10 t CH₄ ≈ 280 t CO₂e.

steps.title: EIA in India
steps.body: Under the EIA Notification 2006, projects are screened (Category A or B), scoped for terms of reference, undergo public consultation, appraisal by an expert appraisal committee and then a decision.

items: Appraisal by the expert appraisal committee
